$comment: Golden test vectors for the table-identity contract. Consumed by BOTH pos_app_client (Dart) and pos_app_server (TypeScript) so the two implementations are proven equal against one fixture rather than by inspection. Derived from the behaviour of pos_app_client/lib/core/utils/reservation_table_availability.dart at tag pre-vynic-saas-full-baseline, which is the stricter and therefore canonical of the two pre-existing implementations. See legacyDivergence below.

encode.$comment: encodeTableCode(floor, tableNumber) -> legacy int code. Every case here is inside the domain both pre-existing implementations already agreed on.

invalid.why: first floor above 10 would encode to 11, which decodes back as second floor table 1
the encoding can only represent two floors
the encoding can only represent two floors

decode.$comment: decodeTableCode(code) -> {floor, tableNumber}. Deliberately total: it validates nothing and both pre-existing implementations behave identically, including for codes that encode would never produce. That behaviour is preserved exactly.

canEncode.$comment: canEncodeTableCode(floor, tableNumber) -> bool. Pickers use this to hide tables the encoding cannot represent, so it decides what is bookable today. It must not change.

cases.note: second floor has no upper bound

tableRef.$comment: The canonical, lossless table reference: 'floor/tableNumber'. Existed only in Dart (core/models/table_ref.dart) before this contract; the TypeScript side is new and additive, so nothing changes on the server by adding it.

encode.note: representable here even though the legacy code cannot express it
third floors are representable here too

decode.note: splits on the FIRST slash only

decodeInvalid.why: separator at position 0, so no floor
separator is the last character, so no table number

legacyDivergence.$comment: The two hand-maintained implementations had ALREADY drifted apart before this contract existed. Recorded here so the convergence is deliberate and reviewable rather than silent. Every input listed is outside the domain of real data: all six TypeScript call sites of encodeTableCode pass WebsiteTable.posFloor / posTableNumber, and the only writer of those columns is BootstrapService.seedWebsiteTables from WEBSITE_TABLE_MAPPINGS, which seeds first floor 1-10 and second floor 1-4 exclusively. Converging on the strict behaviour therefore changes no reachable result.
